Appearance (via video conferencing/physically) 
 
Mr. Shaunak Mitra, Adv. ] For the RP  
Ms. Shreya Choudhary, Adv. ]  
Ms. Rachna Jhunjhunwala, RP ] 
 
 
 
O R D E R 
Per Bidisha Banerjee, Member (Judicial): 
1. This Court convened through hybrid mode of conferencing. 
2. Learned Counsel for the parties were heard in extenso.  
3. This IA(IBC)(LIQ.)/18(KB)2026 has been preferred by Rachna 
Jhunjhunwala, the Resolution Professional of the Corporate 
Debtor to seek the following reliefs, inter alia:   
(a) Condone the delay of three days in filing the instant 
application in view of the reasons mentioned in paragraph 
No. 23.  
(b) To pass necessary order of liquidation of the Shree Badri 
Kedar Udyog Private Limited under Section 33(1)(a) and 
Section 33(2) of the Code, 2016; 
(c) Such further and/or other order or orders as this Hon’ble 
Court may deem fit and proper;        
 
4. Brief facts of the case: 
4.1. An application was filed by the Bank of India (hereinafter 
referred to as the “Financial Creditor”) under Section 7 of the 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 read Rule 6 of the 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating 
Authority) Rules, 2016 against Shree Badri Kedar Udyog 
Private Limited  (hereinafter referred to as the “Corporate 
Debtor”).

Page 3 of 11 
 
4.2. This Tribunal vide its order dated 05.02.2026 admitted the 
application being C.P. (IB)/ 223(KB)2025 for initiation of 
Corporate Insolvency Resolution process against the Corporate 
Debtor and appointed Ms. Rachna Jhunjhunwala as the Interim 
Resolution Professional (“IRP”). In the 1 st CoC Meeting, the IRP 
was confirmed as Resolution Professional w.r.t. Corporate 
Debtor.  
4.3. That the Applicant RP asserted that the public announcement 
in terms of Regulation 6 (1) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy 
Board of India (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate 
Person) Regulation, 2016 (“CIRP Regulations”), was published in 
the newspaper namely “Morning India” ( English) and “Sanmarg” 
(Hindi).  
4.4. The last date for submission of claim was on 19.02.2026 in 
terms of Regulation 6(2) of the said Regulations.  A Claim was 
received from Bank of India as the sole Financial Creditor 
holding 100% of the voting share and the CoC was accordingly 
constituted under Section 21 of the Code on 05.03.2026. 
4.5. That the Applicant / RP published form “G” on 03.04.2026 in 
the newspaper namely Morning India  (English) and Sanmarg 
(Hindi) Ranchi editions, I nviting expression of interest (EoI) for 
submission of resolution plan. However, no EoI was received 
from any interested parties by the last date.

4.9.1. Non-operational status : The Corporate Debtor has been 
wholly non-operational for a period far exceeding three years 
immediately preceding the insolvency commencement date. Its 
account was classified as a non -performing asset on 
30.04.2018, its last audited financial statements ar e for the 
financial year 2016-17 and its registered office has been in the 
occupation of a third party for four to five years. 
4.9.2. Absence of assets : The Corporate Debtor holds no land and 
building, no plant and machinery and no stock. The only asset 
class in respect of which registered valuers could be appointed, 
namely Securities and Financial Assets, has been valued at Nil 
by both valuers. 
4.9.3. Absence of going concern value : The Corporate Debtor was 
engaged in the trading of fabrics and garments. It has no 
employees or workmen, no brand value, no intellectual 
property, no investments yet to mature and no factor 
whatsoever which would bring value as a going concern over 
and above physical assets, of which there are none. 
4.9.4. Absence of market interest : Form G was published on 
03.04.2026 in newspapers having wide circulation and not a 
single Expression of Interest was received by the last date. The 
resolution route stands wholly exhausted. 
4.10. That the Applicant further states that the sole financial creditor 
holding 100% voting share has voted in favour of the resolution

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Insolvency

to submit her consent to act as Liquidator within  10
